extracted.intended_audience: general readers researching the Bill Cosby allegations, litigation, institutional responses, and policy impacts
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style chronology and synthesis of allegations against Bill Cosby, related civil and criminal litigation, institutional actions (rescinded honors, cancellations), public reactions, and legislative responses. The page compiles factual timelines, legal holdings, and examples of policy decisions by organizations and governments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insurance coverage interpretation (ambiguity resolved for insured)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since ambiguous terms are interpreted in favor of coverage, Cosby prevailed. The Court found both the plaintiff's broad interpretation and defendant's narrow interpretation of 'arising out of' reasonable and thus ambiguous, leading to a finding in favor of coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The judge concluded the 'sexual misconduct exclusion' could reasonably be read narrowly or broadly; ambiguity was interpreted in favor of the insured. Also, allegations that are independent of sexual misconduct (e.g., intentionally drugging someone despite rehab history, or statements implying copying claims) may be treated as within policy coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual misconduct exclusion scope as a coverage criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The sexual misconduct exclusion could reasonably be read to require that Dickinson's claims merely relate to sexual misconduct, or that Dickinson's claims be proximately caused by the sexual misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: Whether a claim 'arises out of' sexual misconduct depends on how proximate or directly caused the claimed loss is by the sexual misconduct; courts may parse complaint allegations to find independent causes that place a claim within coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Standards of Conduct as basis for expulsion
rubrics_metrics.description: Cosby and Roman Polanski were expelled from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences 'in accordance with the organization's Standards of Conduct'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations may remove membership or honors when member conduct violates their stated standards; the page cites the Academy invoking its Standards of Conduct to justify expulsions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds used by universities to rescind honorary degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: Many academic institutions rescinded honorary degrees awarded to Cosby, citing Cosby's 2005 deposition and stating the University 'has taken this extraordinary step in light of Mr. Cosby's now-public court depositions that confirm many of the allegations'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universities either relied on new evidence (public depositions) to rescind honors or cited institutional policies (some having no mechanism to rescind). Some institutions stressed they conferred degrees based on information known at the time and lacked a rescission policy; others indicated moral or reputational standards justified rescission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional policy non-rescission as a decision criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Several institutions refused to rescind honorary degrees, often citing 'their policy not to rescind any degree for any reason' or a lack of mechanism to revoke honors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An institution's preexisting policy (forbidding rescission or lacking procedures) can be the controlling criterion in whether to publicly act against a controversial figure, even amid serious allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Amendment / venue admission standard (performers vs. protesters)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Performers should not be able to commandeer a police force ... in order to exclude individuals from the performance because they have a different viewpoint than the performer has", claimed Gloria Allred in suing Cobb County and venue for denying entry to a ticketed protester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal and constitutional challenges can arise when event organizers/performers coordinate with police to exclude ticketed attendees for viewpoint-based reasons; courts consider whether admission policies violate free-speech protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening criminal cases criterion (Oregon bill example)
rubrics_metrics.description: A bill in the Oregon Senate would create an exception to the 12-year statute of limitations for the most serious sex crimes—allowing prosecutors to bring charges if new concrete evidence emerges (e.g., multiple victims coming forward with similar allegations or new written evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative criteria to reopen cases include the presence of new, concrete evidence or corroborating victims; lawmakers debated trade-offs about fairness to accused versus access to justice for victims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative change: eliminating or extending statutes of limitations for sexual offenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Several jurisdictions considered or enacted changes: Nevada repealed the statute of limitations in civil cases related to sexual assault; Nevada extended criminal prosecution for rape from four years to 20 years; California's 'Justice for Victims Act' eliminated the ten-year statute of limitations in California for specified felony sexual offenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy rationale cited by supporters: victims come forward late, and eliminating/extending limits prevents technical bars to prosecution or civil suits. Opponents express concern about evidentiary fairness as time passes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential Medal of Freedom revocation criterion proposed
rubrics_metrics.description: Rep. Paul Gosar drafted a measure to revoke Cosby's Presidential Medal of Freedom on the basis that 'Cosby has admitted to drugging women in order to satisfy his sexual desires, and, therefore, the Federal government should not recognize Cosby with an honor like the Presidential Medal of Freedom.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative proposals for revocation are framed around admissions of serious misconduct and moral unfitness to retain national honors; such proposals may also include penalties for displaying a revoked medal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public and institutional severing of ties as reputational standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerous institutions, colleges, universities, businesses, and broadcast networks severed ties with Cosby (rescinded honors, canceled shows, removed artwork or named programs) in response to allegations; many cited no-tolerance policies on sexual violence or reputational considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations used reputational, ethical, or victim-safety rationales to cut ties—examples include pulling reruns, removing names from programs, canceling appearances, or returning/withholding honors. Some decisions were immediate; others awaited policies or new evidence.
